_comment: How every client frames the home hero, the mockup's proportions (Warren VPN Accueil, 360x640): the hero is 300/360 of its width tall (plus the status bar on a phone), the three registered scenery layers are drawn in one canvas rect, the header floats over the top and the art fades into the page along mask_stops, the mockup's short fade behind the status pill. A framing names a span of canvas rows that must stay clear between the header (clear_top_px) and the point where that fade reaches half opacity (clear_bottom_fraction of the hero height, given to the formula as fade_px = height * (1 - clear_bottom_fraction)): the cameras, the whole burrow and Bula down to his shins whenever he is out (ground), the country's skyline down to the top of the burrow once he is in (sky). The canvas is drawn at width-fit unless the span cannot fit, then it narrows and centres. Its top sits flush with the hero top when it can; it drops (headroom) only when a skyline would otherwise sit under the header, and rises only when the span bottom would pass the half-opacity point. The rows above a dropped canvas, and the columns beside a narrowed one, take the landscape's topFill from scenery.json, and the canvas edges facing them are feathered over feather_rows canvas rows.

ground.provenance: top_row: 10 rows above the higher camera (plaine.webp, the left camera housing starts at row 330). bottom_row: Bula's shins (bula.webp, his body spans rows 427 to 1124), below the burrow mouth (rows 759 to 920); with the canvas at width-fit this puts the cameras where the mockup draws them.

sky.top_row: skylineTopRow of the landscape in scenery.json
sky.provenance: bottom_row: the top of the burrow mouth (row 759): every flag (rows 427 to about 620) lies inside.

formula: hero_height = hero_width * hero_height_ratio (+ the status bar inset on a phone)
y_min = clear_top_px - span_top * scale ; y_max = clear_bottom - span_bottom * scale
the hero's alpha follows mask_stops ([fraction of the hero height, alpha]) from its top to its bottom
